# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/server"
```

Package server is the controlled station of IEC 60870-5-102, the integrated total station (a meter or data concentrator): the secondary station of unbalanced transmission. It answers the link procedures of the controlling station and serves the standard read commands from a [Store](#type-store) of records:

  - C\_RD\_NA\_2 with P\_MP\_NA\_2 (cause 5), from [Config.ProductSpec](#func-config-productspec);
  - C\_TI\_NA\_2 with M\_TI\_TA\_2 (cause 5), from [Config.Clock](#func-config-clock);
  - C\_CI\_NA\_2 .. C\_CI\_NU\_2 with the activation confirmation (cause 7), the selected integration periods as M\_IT\_TA\_2 .. M\_IT\_TM\_2 (cause 5) and the activation termination (cause 10);
  - C\_SP\_NA\_2 and C\_SP\_NB\_2 the same way with M\_SP\_TA\_2.

A request it cannot serve is mirrored with a cause of refusal: 16 for a record address the store does not hold, 14 for a record without integrated totals of the requested family (or an unknown type without a [Handler](#type-handler)), 18 when no integration period matches, 17 when the address range selects no total. These procedures and the choice of causes are interpretations of the Beckhoff TS650x manual (section 9.1.11 names the causes) and of the recorded traffic; see docs/iec102/INTEROPERABILITY.md.

Every other ASDU (the REE profile's session, clock setting and tariff requests, private types) goes to the [Handler](#type-handler), which answers through [Server.Send](#func-server-send) and [Server.Mirror](#func-server-mirror). Answers are class 2 data: the controlling stations we compare with (gisce/iec870ree, daiiniel/IEC60870-5-102) poll class 2 only.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Link holds the link options; Link.FT12 is set from LinkAddrSize.
	Link link.Config
	// LinkAddrSize is the size of the link address field: 1 or 2 octets,
	// [iec102.NoLinkAddr] for none. Zero means
	// [iec102.DefaultLinkAddrSize].
	LinkAddrSize int
	// LinkAddr is this station's link address.
	LinkAddr uint16
	// CommonAddr is the common address of ASDU (measuring point address)
	// this station serves; requests to another are refused with cause 16.
	CommonAddr uint16
	// Params are the codec parameters.
	Params iec102.Params

	// ProductSpec answers C_RD_NA_2.
	ProductSpec iec102.ProductSpec
	// Store holds the records the server serves. Nil serves none.
	Store *Store
	// Clock returns the station's time for C_TI_NA_2. Nil means time.Now.
	// A Clock that does not return normally closes the server, as for the
	// Handler.
	Clock func() time.Time

	// Handler handles the other control-direction ASDUs. Nil refuses them
	// with cause 14.
	Handler Handler
	// QueueSize bounds the class 2 queue. Zero means [DefaultQueueSize].
	QueueSize int
	// OnState is called with each change of the link state: from the
	// station's link goroutine on a reset of remote link, and from Close
	// for StateClosed. It must return quickly. It may call Close, which
	// then does not wait for the link goroutine. An OnState that does not
	// return normally is logged and closes the server, as for the Handler.
	OnState func(s iec102.State, err error)
	// Logger receives the log entries; nil is silent.
	Logger iec60870.Logger
}
```

Config configures a server.

### type Handler

```go
type Handler interface {
	HandleASDU(s *Server, a *iec102.ASDU)
}
```

Handler handles the control-direction ASDUs the server does not answer itself. Calls are made one at a time from a goroutine of the server; the handler answers through the Server, whose methods it may call. Close from the handler does not wait for the handler's goroutine: it returns at once, and the close completes when the handler has returned. A handler that does not return normally is logged with its stack and closes the server; [Server.Err](#func-server-err) reports it.

The ASDU is the handler's own: a new one is decoded for each call and the server keeps no reference to it, so the handler may keep or modify it.

#### func New

New starts a server on rw. Close stops it and closes rw when it is an io.Closer.

#### func (Server) Close

```go
func (s *Server) Close() error
```

Close stops the station. Close is safe to call more than once and from several goroutines: the first call closes the transport and returns its error; later calls return nil.

Called from the Handler, the Clock or OnState, Close cannot wait for the goroutine it runs on: it stops the server and returns nil at once, and the close completes, StateClosed reported included, when that callback has returned.

#### func (Server) Done

```go
func (s *Server) Done() <-chan struct{}
```

Done is closed when the station stops: after Close, a transport failure, or a callback that did not return normally. Err tells which.

#### func (Server) Err

```go
func (s *Server) Err() error
```

Err returns the error that stopped the station: the transport's, or that of a callback that did not return normally (wrapping [iec102.ErrClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102#ErrClosed)); nil while it runs or after Close.

### type Store

```go
type Store struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Store holds the records a server serves: integration periods of integrated totals and single-point information, per record address. It is safe for concurrent use; the application adds to it while the server runs.

#### func NewStore

```go
func NewStore() *Store
```

NewStore returns an empty store.

#### func (Store) AddPeriod

```go
func (s *Store) AddPeriod(record uint8, p iec102.IntegratedTotals)
```

AddPeriod adds the integrated totals of one integration period to record address record. p.T (M\_IT\_TA\_2 .. M\_IT\_TM\_2) is the type it is served as, p.Time the end of the period. Periods are kept in the order added, which should be oldest first: "the oldest integration period" of C\_CI\_NA\_2 and its siblings is the first one added of its family.

#### func (Store) AddSinglePoints

```go
func (s *Store) AddSinglePoints(record uint8, pts ...iec102.SinglePoint)
```

AddSinglePoints adds single-point information to record address record (normally a list address 50..55).
